cross_market_insights: Weak SERP everywhere: positions 1 to 3 are Pinterest pins, an Etsy listing, a Facebook post and a 2020 brand blog. No authoritative editorial list holds the top spot in any market.

In all three AU cities our own /expert-advice/destination-wedding-checklist already ranks #3 on a single packing line. A dedicated list from the same domain should be able to take that slot; the checklist must then link to the new list so the two do not compete.
Strong printable intent: Etsy printables and 'PDF' offers appear in every image pack. A printable, sectioned list is what searchers want.
Nobody splits the list by who packs it (couple, guests, wedding-day kit, documents, carry-on). Most are bride-only.

Nobody covers Australian rules: biosecurity on return (flowers, food, natural items), medicines (TGA, Smartraveller), lithium batteries (CASA), Border Force duty-free and cash. All results are US or UK generic.
No luxury angle: nothing on what a planner or advisor handles so the couple does not pack it (steaming on site, welcome bags sourced locally, decor shipped or hired), or on insuring rings and gown.
PAA leans to guests (what not to wear, out-of-town etiquette) and to the bride's day-of bag; we have live pages for both to link.

Volumes are tiny in Australia (10/mo for each destination variant; 40/mo for 'wedding packing list'). Value is in cluster coverage, image search and Pinterest, and as a conversion asset, not raw traffic.
payload.recommended_angle: The printable destination wedding packing list for Australians, split by who packs what (couple, guests, wedding-day kit, documents and carry-on), with the Australian travel rules linked at the claim and a clear line between what you pack and what your Wedded Advisor arranges on the ground.
